claims.text: The starting high-entropy-alloy components have native oxide surface films.
A thin, uniform, nanostructured MoS2 coating can be deposited on the alloy surface by physical vapor deposition or a similar method.
The MoS2 coating will produce an in-situ lubricious tribolayer during operation.
The tribolayer will form at the coating/alloy interface during frictional contact.
Mechanical stress and thermal activation will cause the MoS2 coating to reorient into a low-shear tribolayer.
The low-shear tribolayer will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact.
Minimizing direct metal-to-metal contact will decrease the coefficient of friction.
The MoS2-derived tribolayer will act as a barrier to mechanical wear.
Relative to untreated high-entropy alloys, MoS2-coated samples will reduce the coefficient of friction by more than 30%.
Relative to untreated high-entropy alloys, MoS2-coated samples will exhibit a significant reduction in wear rate.
The coating will reduce friction and wear from room temperature to approximately 600°C under cyclic mechanical loading.
Effectiveness requires adequate adhesion of the MoS2 coating to the high-entropy-alloy substrate.
Effectiveness requires the coating to withstand repeated thermal cycling and mechanical stresses.
Insufficient coating thickness may cause failure of the intervention.
Operating above the phase-stability limit of MoS2 may cause failure of the intervention.
Long-term adhesion and durability under prolonged cyclic thermal and mechanical loading are uncertain.
